Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase! The umpires and players are all out in the middle. Stafanie Taylor and Hayley Matthews are the openers for West Indies Women! Rachel Slater has the new ball and will start the proceedings for Scotland Women! Away we go..
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, the West Indies Women have done a super job here. Now, the onus is on their batters to chase this down and record their first win of the campaign. Scotland Women will surely need to come in with the right intent from the get go. A few early wickets, and they could certainly be in the game here. Do join us for the second essay shortly.

Chinelle Henry is in for a quick chat. She says it feels good to give a strong start at the top and they as a team did well to restrict the opposition to a lower total. Talks about the fielding lapses and says it is a bit disappointing but they did manage to get the job done with the ball. Talks about the previous loss and says this is a good chance to get their net run rate up but they will have to look at winning it.

Kathryn Bryce and Ailsa Lister then steadied the ship, taking Scotland to 45/2 at the 10-over mark. West Indies, however, maintained pressure with tight bowling. Post the halfway mark, Scotland Women tried to up the ante, but could not really make it count. West Indies bowler's were in sublime form especially Afy Fletcher who picked up two wickets in two deliveries. Kathryn Bryce tries her best to hold the innings together while wickets kept tumbling at the other end, although once Bryce was dismissed, Scotland’s hopes of a recovery faded, as none of the remaining batters could provide stability or accelerate the scoring. The consistent fall of wickets stalled any momentum, leaving them unable to post a challenging total.

Scotland’s innings got off to a shaky start in their Women's T20 World Cup match against West Indies, losing both openers early within four balls. Saskia Horley hit two quick boundaries but fell soon after, followed by Sarah Bryce, leaving them at 25/2 at the end of the Powerplay.

A dominating performance from West Indies Women with the ball in hand. They never really allowed the Scotland batters to grow in this contest. The bowlers were just incredible in the death overs, and have done their job brilliantly in the first innings. Despite winning the toss, Scotland Women could not really turn up with the bat in hand.

OUT! TIMBER! Chinelle Henry joins the party and Scotland Women lose both the openers! Henry comes from over the wicket and lands it on a nagging length on middle and off and gets the ball to skid through a bit off the deck. Sarah Bryce makes room and looks to force her push through the off but the ball just beats her bat and goes through to rattle the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Chinelle Henry to Sarah Bryce, OUT! b Chinelle Henry.

Commentary.Commentary: Charges in at the stumps on a good length, Sarah Bryce tucks it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Chinelle Henry to Sarah Bryce, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and outside off, Sarah Bryce looks to drive but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Chinelle Henry to Sarah Bryce, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on off, Sarah Bryce pushes it straight down the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Chinelle Henry to Sarah Bryce, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kathryn Bryce walks out to bat at number 3 for Scotland Women!

OUT! CAUGHT! A great catch from Deandra Dottin and West Indies Women draw first blood! Hayley Matthews gives the ball some air and keeps it full, on middle, Saskia Horley takes a step out and looks to hoick it across the line but mistimes it in the air and over mid-wicket. Deandra Dottin backtracks a few steps and then swivels to take a great catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Deandra Dottin b Hayley Matthews
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Hayley Matthews to Saskia Horley, OUT! c Deandra Dottin b Hayley Matthews.

Hayley Matthews drags the length down and lands it on middle, Saskia Horley rocks back and pulls it to the right of square leg who fails to stop the ball. The fielder from deep mid-wicket charges to the ball but fails to pull it back in time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Hayley Matthews to Saskia Horley, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Comes from over the wicket and drifts it into the pads, on middle and leg, Sarah Bryce tucks it to square leg for a single.

On a length, well outside off, Saskia Horley looks to free her arms and tries to reach for it away from her body but misses.

This is on a length and on off, Sarah Bryce looks to drive it away on the off but gets a thick outside edge that flies over to the left of the first slip. Matthews times her jump and gets a hand to it but it just doesn't stick. The batters cross.

Commentary.Commentary: Saskia Horley and Scotland Women are underway! Henry steams in from over the wicket and hurls it on a hard length, on off with a hint of away shape, Saskia Horley looks to push it with a straight bat but gets an outside edge to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Chinelle Henry to Saskia Horley, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: All pre-match formalities are now behind us, and the stage is set for the action to commence! The umpires make their way out to the middle. West Indies Women are in a tight huddle alongside the ropes with some final pep talks from skipper Hayley Matthews before they spread out in the field. Sarah Bryce and Saskia Horley are the openers for Scotland Women! It will be Chinelle Henry to start the proceedings with the ball in hand. Away we go..
Right then, both the teams stride out to the middle and line-up for their respective national anthems. It will be Scotland's first. Followed by West Indies' anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Natalie Germanos is down at the centre for the pitch report. She says the square boundaries are even and the straight hit is bigger which the players will need to keep in mind. WV Raman joins her and says the pitch is a bit slow and the bowlers will try to take pace off. Mentions that the biggest concern will be fielding under lights and that will be crucial.

Hayley Matthews, the captain of West Indies Women is in for a chat. She starts by saying that they need to pick themselves up after the first match. Hopes that they can go out and have a positive performance tonight. Adds that she is happy to have Stefani back fit in the side. Ends by saying that they have made two changes to the side.

Kathryn Bryce, the skipper of Scotland says they will look to put a good total and then look to defend. Mentions the outfield is bigger here and they will have to hit those pockets and run hard. Adds that they want to stay ahead in the game as much as possible with the bat and that will be key. Says the conditions are a little different but it's cooler. Concludes that they go unchanged.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews (C), Qiana Joseph, Stafanie Taylor, Deandra Dottin, Shemaine Alteia Campbelle (WK), Chinelle Henry, Aaliyah Alleyne, Chedean Nation (In for Zaida James), Afy Fletcher, Karishma Ramharack, Ashmini Munisar (In for Shamilia Connell).

Scotland Women (Unchanged playing XI) - Saskia Horley, Sarah Bryce (WK), Kathryn Bryce (C), Ailsa Lister, Priyanaz Chatterji, Darcey Carter, Lorna Jack, Katherine Fraser, Rachel Slater, Abtaha Maqsood, Olivia Bell.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of Scotland Women. They will BAT first.

In other news, India Women were able to get the better of Pakistan Women in the afternoon match. India won the game by 6 wickets. With this victory, India now will be hoping to grow in this competition with the momentum on their side. Also, as there was a slight delay for the afternoon game to finish. This game between West Indies Women and Scotland Women will be starting on 2.05 pm GMT. Just a 5 minute delay caused by it.

... MATCH DAY ...

In a pivotal Group B encounter of the Women's World T20, West Indies will face Scotland, as both teams will be seeking to bounce back from heavy defeats in their opening matches. Scotland suffered a significant loss to Bangladesh, while West Indies fell to last year's finalists, South Africa. West Indies cannot afford consecutive losses, particularly to Scotland. Conversely, Scotland will aim for a comprehensive performance against West Indies, who they recently defeated in a warm-up match. A victory is essential for both teams to secure valuable points and regain momentum in the tournament. In their tournament opener, the West Indies women's team suffered a disappointing 10-wicket defeat to South Africa, marked by a lackluster batting display and ineffective bowling. Only Stefanie Taylor managed to contribute significantly with a score of 44, leading the team to a modest total of 118. The rest of the batting lineup faltered, with key players like Hayley Matthews, Qiana Joseph, Deandra Dottin, and Shemaine Campbelle failing to adapt to the conditions and losing their wickets to loose shots against the South African spinners. In the bowling department, the West Indies struggled to make inroads, as South Africa's openers, Wolvaardt and Brits, built a solid partnership without facing much pressure. Despite Matthews employing eight bowlers, none were able to secure a breakthrough, allowing South Africa to chase down the target comfortably. On the flip side, Scotland's debut match in the Women’s World T20 against Bangladesh didn't go as planned. After a challenging start in the field, where key catches were dropped under tough conditions, Scottish bowlers, led by captain Kathryn Bell and spinners Olivia Bell and Katherine Fraser, managed to create pressure by taking crucial wickets. Saskia Horley stood out in the latter part of the innings, claiming three wickets in her final overs, helping restrict Bangladesh to a manageable total. However, Scotland's batting response faltered. Despite a gritty 49 off 52 balls from Sarah Bryce, who maintained her composure after keeping wickets for 20 overs, the rest of the batting lineup struggled to build partnerships and lost wickets at regular intervals. To be competitive in future matches, Scotland's batters must adopt a more aggressive approach and form partnerships to chase down par totals effectively. So, which side are you backing?
